coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

names: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P27
record.summary: Parcel P27 in OCII's Mission Bay open-space plan: the Long-Range Property Management Plan lists it as lot 8723-002 (15,246 sq ft) at the northwest corner of Owens and Mariposa Streets. Pier & Point's outline is a small triangular wedge of about 1,029 m2 between the I-280 ramp and Owens St, about 86% inside that Assessor lot, drawn by hand rather than taken from the lot's boundary. OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P27' among the parcels Rec and Park will manage "when built"; no source read says it has been built, and in USDA NAIP imagery viewed 2026-09-29 the ground is a strip of dry grass and bare ground.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- an outline drawn by hand, traced as the leftover ground between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes; not a surveyed footprint or a parcel line. About 86% of it lies inside Assessor lot 8723002, the lot OCII's Long-Range Property Management Plan names for parcel P27, but it covers only 61% of that lot (1,029 m2 of 1,457 m2), so the lot's own lines are not used. Its west side is cut along the continuation of the curved west edge of the Assessor lot to its north (The Exchange on 16th), because the rest of the earlier shape lay over I-280 ramp lanes; that edge is an extension of the lot line, not a traced boundary. Shown as planned: no source read says the parcel has been built.
notes.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and neighbouring mapped shapes near the UCSF Medical Center campus, picked by hand by Pier & Point from a numbered map of such leftover pieces, not taken from a surveyed parcel. The chosen piece was then cut further by hand: it forks into two thin parallel strips (~13-21m wide, running north alongside a building courtyard) above a wider single base (up to 46m wide); the base was kept and both forks were dropped.

open_questions: Whether this parcel has been built is not known. OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation (slide 5) lists 'P27' among the parcels Rec and Park will manage "when built"; no later source read says it was built. USDA NAIP imagery viewed 2026-09-29 shows a strip of dry grass and bare ground here, which is not a source for completion either way.

The outline is a hand-drawn approximation, not the lot. About 86% of it lies inside Assessor lot 8723002, the lot OCII's plan names for P27, but it covers only 61% of that lot (1,029 m2 of 1,457 m2; the plan gives 15,246 sq ft, about 1,416 m2).
No source read gives this parcel a name beyond 'P27', or says who would operate it other than the September 2023 presentation's "RPD will manage ... P27 when built".
